run.question: Which service has the most error events in the events collection? What is the most common error code for that service and how many times does it appear?

report.summary: Querying the only collection in the configured MongoDB database (opsdb.events, 200 documents estimated), error-level events (level="error") total 133 of 200; the remaining 67 are level="info". Grouping those 133 error events by the service field returns five services whose counts sum to 133, so no error event lacked a service value: payment-processor 47, inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18, search-indexer 12. payment-processor therefore has the most error events. Grouping payment-processor's error events by error_code returns three codes summing to its 47 events: TXN-4821 "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response" 23, TXN-5190 "Currency conversion service unavailable" 14, TXN-3007 "Duplicate transaction ID detected" 10. The most common error code for payment-processor is TXN-4821, appearing 23 times. Caveats: these counts describe the stored collection at query time; the payment-processor error documents I read carry timestamps from 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T00:46:00, which is outside the authorized window (2026-11-21T10:15:38Z to 2026-11-22T10:15:38Z), so they are not evidence about that window. The service values in this collection (e.g. payment-processor) are different identifiers from the Jaeger service names (e.g. payment), and no mapping between them was verified, so this finding says nothing about the health of the Jaeger service named payment.

claims.text: The configured MongoDB database opsdb contains exactly one collection, named events.
The events collection's fields are _id, error_code, level, message, service and timestamp, with an estimated document count of 200 and only the default _id index.
Grouping the events collection by level returns level="error" 133 documents and level="info" 67 documents (sum 200).

Grouping level="error" documents by service returns payment-processor 47, inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18 and search-indexer 12; these five counts sum to the full 133 error documents, so payment-processor is the service with the most error events.

For service payment-processor with level="error", the error_code counts are TXN-4821 23, TXN-5190 14 and TXN-3007 10 (sum 47), so TXN-4821 is the most common error code for that service with 23 occurrences.

Grouping payment-processor error documents by error_code together with message returns TXN-4821 = "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response" (23), TXN-5190 = "Currency conversion service unavailable" (14), TXN-3007 = "Duplicate transaction ID detected" (10).

The 47 payment-processor error documents have timestamps ranging from 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T00:46:00, which lies outside the authorized window 2026-11-21T10:15:38Z to 2026-11-22T10:15:38Z.

The three newest payment-processor error documents returned (sorted by timestamp descending) are all error_code TXN-3007 with message "Duplicate transaction ID detected", timestamped 2025-12-01T00:46:00, 2025-12-01T00:45:00 and 2025-12-01T00:44:00.

Against treating this as an incident-window finding: the events collection's documents carry level=info for 67 of 200 records and its error documents are dated 2025-12-01, so the collection does not describe the authorized 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-22 window, and no document in it was observed inside that window.

gaps: The events collection's timestamps (2025-12-01) fall outside the authorized window (2026-11-21T10:15:38Z to 2026-11-22T10:15:38Z), so the counts describe the stored collection as of query time and cannot be attributed to the incident window.

The service identifiers in the events collection (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) do not match the Jaeger service names available for tracing (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping); no mapping between the two naming schemes was verified, so the collection's counts were not cross-checked against trace or metric error signals.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change record was consulted.
Only the events collection exists in the configured database, so no other collection could corroborate these error counts.
next_steps: If these error events are meant to describe the incident window, confirm the timezone/clock of whatever writes to opsdb.events, since the stored documents are stamped 2025-12-01.
Confirm whether events.service values such as payment-processor correspond to the Jaeger service name payment before correlating these counts with trace or metric error data.
